text:
sara: Quick run started: cascade-attn steering sweep across A100/H100/L40S. Policy: prefer paged-fusion for seq >= 2048, fallback to fused-flash for short seq. Using batch-size sweep [1,2,4,8,16]. Will post trimmed results.

mike: small nit — the policy change also adds a kv-prefetch threshold at 512 tokens (warm prefixes). Decided to be conservative for now.

bench-bot: run summary (trimmed):
A100 | seq=256  bsz=8  : 1.8 ms/token
A100 | seq=1024 bsz=8  : 2.9 ms/token
H100 | seq=256  bsz=8  : 1.6 ms/token
H100 | seq=1024 bsz=8  : 3.8 ms/token  <-- unexpected regression vs previous baseline 2.7 ms/token
L40S | seq=1024 bsz=4  : 4.1 ms/token

ciara: who owns the kernel-policy changes? could this be a selector bug for the H100 memcopy path?

raj: added profiler traces for the H100 failing case, looks like an extra memcpy during kv spill at step 3. snippet:
```trace
copy_kernel: 2.1ms
attn_kernel_fused: 0.6ms
paging_eviction: 0.9ms
```

sara: repro on my devbox (H100): attaching capture. Also saw higher PCIe stall counters on the failing runs.

mike: hypothesis: cascaded selector prefers paged-fusion but misidentifies cache warmness, triggering extra kv spill. Try forcing fused-flash for seq <= 2048 on H100 and compare.

sara: quick forced run applied -> H100 seq=1024 bsz=8 now 2.5 ms/token. That matches baseline. Patch looks promising. I'll open a PR with a minimal failing test and rollback the selector fallback for H100 until we have a safer warmness check.

ciara: add a unit test that simulates mixed-prefix lengths and randomized batch arrivals; QA should run bursty arrivals with batch jitter to catch selector oscillations.

sara: :thumbsup: will do. tagging @mike to review the selector fix.

mike: will review. rollout notes: canary to 5% dedicated first. Monitor latency P50/P95/P99, KV eviction rate, and PCIe stall counters. If any regression at P99 or eviction rate > baseline + 10%, rollback.

bench-bot: posted full CSV and perf traces to s3://redwood-bench/cascade-attn/4381234567-results.csv

sara: thanks all — closing the loop after PR is up and canary looks green.
